constraints: denominators of degree at most 1 here; integer excluded values
hints: A rational expression is undefined where its denominator equals zero.
Set the monomial or binomial denominator equal to zero before simplifying any other part.
Solve that denominator equation and record the input that must be excluded.

objective: Solve a linear denominator equal to zero
constraints: denominators of the form ax + b with small integer a and b; the excluded value is an integer or a simple fraction
hints: The excluded input is the x-value that would make the linear denominator zero.
Write the denominator equation ax plus b equals zero.
Undo the constant and divide by the coefficient; keep a fractional solution exact when it occurs.

objective: Factor, then cancel a common binomial
constraints: numerator is a difference of squares or a monic trinomial; the denominator is one of its linear factors; the answer is a binomial
hints: Factor the numerator completely so its linear factors are visible.
Identify the binomial factor shared with the denominator and cancel that factor, not individual terms.
Write the remaining factor as the simplified expression while retaining the original restriction.

constraints: numerator and denominator both factor into linear binomials with integer roots; exactly one factor cancels
hints: Factor both numerator and denominator into linear binomials before attempting cancellation.
Cancel the one identical factor shared across the fraction bar.
Multiply or leave the noncancelled factors in the requested simple form, with the original domain restriction preserved.

constraints: coefficients at most 12; results must reduce to a single fraction
hints: Multiply numerators together and denominators together to form one fraction.
Cancel common variable factors using exponent rules before doing unnecessary expansion.
Reduce the numerical coefficient and leave the result as one simplified monomial fraction.

constraints: one factor needs a difference of squares or a monic trinomial factored first; exactly one binomial cancels
hints: Factor the expression that is not already written as linear factors.
Before multiplying, cancel the matching binomial that appears once above and once below the fraction bars.
Multiply only the remaining factors and keep the given restrictions from the original denominators.

constraints: a factor of each numerator cancels against a factor of the other denominator; cancel before multiplying, never expand
hints: Factor numerators and denominators enough to expose identical factors across the two fractions.
Cross-cancel common factors before multiplying; never cancel terms joined by addition.
Multiply the reduced numerical factors and any leftover factors to form the simplified result.

constraints: flip-and-multiply; every quotient cancels to a simple monomial fraction
hints: Division by a rational expression means multiply by its reciprocal.
Rewrite the divisor by exchanging its numerator and denominator, then change division to multiplication.
Cancel common monomial factors and reduce coefficients after the flip-and-multiply step.

constraints: flip the divisor, then cancel matching linear binomials; no trinomials at this level
hints: Keep the first rational expression unchanged and replace the divisor with its reciprocal.
Factor or identify matching binomials across the resulting product, then cancel whole matching factors.
Multiply what remains and retain every stated restriction from the original expressions.

constraints: one numerator is a monic trinomial factoring over the integers; flip, factor, then cancel
hints: Convert the division into multiplication by the reciprocal before simplifying.
Factor the monic trinomial into its two linear binomials, then expose any common factor with the flipped divisor.
Cancel only complete matching factors and write the remaining expression on the original domain.

constraints: every numerator and denominator factors into linear binomials with integer roots; the answer is one reduced fraction
hints: Factor every numerator and denominator into linear factors before cancelling anything.
Treat the expression as one product and cancel matching factors across fraction bars.
Multiply the unreduced factors only after all possible cancellation, while preserving the original-domain exclusions.

constraints: flip the divisor first, then factor all four parts; monic quadratics with integer roots only
hints: Change the division sign to multiplication by the reciprocal of the entire divisor first.
Factor all four numerator and denominator parts, even those that look likely to cancel.
Cancel complete shared binomials and simplify the resulting product without introducing new domain values.

objective: Add and subtract over one denominator
constraints: identical denominators (a monomial or one linear binomial); combine the numerators only, no LCD building
hints: Because the denominators match exactly, keep that denominator unchanged.
Combine only the numerators using the indicated addition or subtraction.
Simplify the new numerator if possible, then retain the common denominator and its restriction.
